4c177718.mechanism: 15x15 input: a legend band above a grey divider row 5 holds a blue (1) 3x3 sprite at cols 2-4, a red (2) T/inverted-T arrow at cols 6-8 and a second-colour 3x3 sprite at cols 10-12; below the divider a copy of the blue sprite sits at (6+brow+3*(1-cdir), bcol). The 9x15 output is the area below the divider with the coloured sprite stacked directly above or below the blue copy depending on the arrow orientation (cdir).
4c177718.fixture_evidence: 6 canonical pairs (4 train, 2 test), all 15x15 -> 9x15. Pair 0 (cdir=1, bar on top, line 49 writes row 1) puts the 7-sprite below the blue copy; pair 1 (cdir=0) puts the 4-sprite above. Blue is colour 1 and the arrow colour 2 in every pair; the lower blue copy is at bcol 1,5,6,5,1,8 i.e. never col 0 and never 12.

dimensions.why: Canvas 15x15 and output 15x9 are literals (line 45); output height is H-6 because the divider is fixed at row 5 (line 47). The stacking rule only needs a lower region at least 6 rows tall and wide enough for a 3-wide sprite; nothing in the rule refers to 15. Generalising also requires the factory, which hard-codes legend offset 8 and step 3 (factory qx = x - 8*RV), to be revisited.

objects.why: Both sprites come from diagonally_connected_sprite() 3x3 (common.conway_sprite never deletes a full row/column, so bounding box is always 3x3). The fixed 3x3 box is rule-supported because the stacking offset of 3 rows (lines 55-56) equals sprite height; sprite size itself (3) is incidental, and only one blue/one coloured pair is ever present.

placement.why: Legend positions (cols 2-4, 6-8, 10-12, rows 1-3) are fixed literals, incidental to the rule. brow 0..3 is exactly what fits two stacked 3-row sprites in 9 rows (rule-supported given the canvas); bcol 1..11 excludes col 0 and col 12, both of which fit (incidental).

density_colours.why: Second sprite colour is random excluding 1,2,5 (rule-supported: it must differ from blue, arrow and divider). Blue=1, arrow=2, divider=5 are fixed role colours in source and in all fixtures; the native domain therefore has 7 colour variants only; the factory palette permutation (P[1],P[2],P[5]) is the only colour-role variation.

rule_parameters.why: cdir is the single binary rule parameter (arrow orientation -> above/below); both values are sampled uniformly and both appear in fixtures.

demonstration_context.why: Each input carries its own arrow cue, so the output is determined from the query alone once the arrow-to-direction convention is learnt; any episode with both cdir values in train shows the convention. Factory derives the direction from the T's projection counts (nmin vs nmax), not from demonstrations.

4c177718.proposal: Parameterise lower-region height (>=6) and width (>=4) and place legend columns relative to W, widen bcol to 0..W-3; keep the 3x3 sprite and cdir semantics. Any change to legend spacing needs the factory's hard-coded 8-column legend offset updated in lockstep and recertification. Not urgent relative to families with tiny domains: 128/128 audit inputs are unique.
4c177718.uncertainties: Whether the arrow semantics generalise to non-3x3 sprites was not checked; factory changes are needed for any legend-layout change and were not attempted.

4cd1b7b2.mechanism: A random 4x4 Latin square over colours 1..4, built row by row with column-conflict rejection (48-59). Then 5 or 6 cells are blanked to 0, one per still-complete row or column, in shuffled strip order (61-78). The output fills the blanks back by propagating lines with exactly three values (27-46, 86).
4cd1b7b2.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs (3 train, 1 test), 4x4, blank counts 5, 5, 6, 6 (probe), exactly the native 5..6. Probe: 1993 distinct inputs in 2000 draws, blanks 5/6 in 1015/985. Audit 128/128 unique, 125 orbits; certificate 999/1000.

dimensions.why: 4x4 is tied to the four symbols 1..4 (52) and to the sum-to-10 completion (35, 42). An n x n square with n colours would change the colour roles and the arithmetic, so keeping the 4x4 Latin geometry is defensible. It is the one rule-tied restriction here; the blank count is not.

objects.why: A 4x4 Latin square over four symbols is the task; rows avoid column clashes (56).

placement.why: Blank positions are random. Blanking only complete strips means zeros can be undone in reverse order, so single-line propagation always solves the input; that is rule-supporting.

density_colours.why: The constructor forces exactly 5 or 6 blanks (75-78). The rule only needs a completion that line propagation determines. Probe: the constructor's own strip scheme reaches 1..7 blanks, and the constructor solver and the factory restore the square in every case (e.g. 495/495 at 1 blank, 34/34 at 7). The fixtures' 5, 5, 6, 6 are fixture-only counts. Colours 1..4 on 0 stay roles.

rule_parameters.why: Fill the unique missing symbol of a line.

demonstration_context.why: The factory reads demonstration outputs only for non-4x4 grids (to collect colours), which never occur natively; on 4x4 it uses palette colours and deduction.

4cd1b7b2.proposal: Medium. Sample the blank count over the propagation-solvable range (the strip scheme reaches 1..7; or blank more cells and keep scenes whose propagation completes uniquely). Keep 4x4 and colours 1..4. Recertify.
4cd1b7b2.uncertainties: Whether 1-2 blank scenes are useful (valid but near-trivial). Blank counts above 7 need a different blanking scheme plus a uniqueness check, so solvability is not shown here.

4e469f39.mechanism: One or two grey (5) hollow 4-wide boxes of height 3-5 each have a one-cell gap in the top edge at col+1 or col+2; the output fills the interior red (2), fills the gap red, and draws a red line on the row above the box from the gap toward the side opposite the gap's half (left=0 -> rightward, left=1 -> leftward) to the grid edge.
4e469f39.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 10x10. Pair 0 (left=0, gap col 4) line runs cols 4-9 on row 2; pair 1 (left=1, gap col 5) line runs cols 0-5; pairs 2/3 have two boxes with the second box's line on the row between them (row 6). Only colours 0,5 in inputs.

dimensions.why: Canvas is grids(10, 10) and the row bound 10 appears at lines 35 and 41; the line-to-edge rule (line 53 uses 10) works for any canvas wide enough for the box.

objects.why: Box width is fixed at 4 (hollow_rect width 4, line 47): a 2-wide interior makes the gap side a clean binary cue, so width 4 is rule-supporting for the left/right decision; a wider box would need a 'gap left/right of centre' rule. Heights 3-5 and at most 2 boxes are incidental to the 10-row canvas.

placement.why: row >= 1 keeps a row above the box for the red line (rule-supported); two boxes are vertically stacked with a 1-2 row gap so the lower box's line lies between them (rule-supporting non-collision). Columns 1..5 exclude col 0 and col 6 which also fit a width-4 box (incidental); boxes are never side by side.

density_colours.why: Wall grey 5, fill red 2 and background 0 are literals and fixed in all fixtures; the factory varies them by palette permutation only.

rule_parameters.why: The only rule parameter is the gap side per box, sampled independently per box, so two-box inputs can show both directions.

demonstration_context.why: The direction is a fixed convention read from each box's gap; any pair with left=0 and one with left=1 teaches it. Single-box episodes can show only one side if all draws agree (probability ~1/2 per single-box pair); episode coverage not measured.

4e469f39.proposal: Sample H,W independently (e.g. 6-20), allow col 0..W-4 and more than two boxes at non-overlapping row bands (each needs a free row above). Keep width 4 unless the verifier is generalised to a centre-relative gap. Domain is small (audit 120 unique inputs / 106 orbits of 128; source admits roughly 150 single-box plus a few thousand two-box configurations), so a modest canvas parameterisation adds real variety. Recertify.
4e469f39.uncertainties: Domain size estimate is a hand count from lines 31-43, not enumerated. Whether lines from two side-by-side boxes may cross (if boxes were allowed in the same rows) is undefined by fixtures.

4f537728.mechanism: A 7x7 lattice of 2x2 blue (1) blocks with period 3 (offset 0 or 1 in each axis) on a 20x20 canvas; one block (row, col in 1..5) has another colour. The output recolours every block sharing that block's lattice row or column.
4f537728.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, all 20x20. Pair 0 (row 5, col 4, offsets 1/1) shows partial first row/col blocks and an empty last row/col; the coloured row and column are painted in the output across the whole lattice including partial blocks.

dimensions.why: 20x20 canvas and 7x7 lattice are literals; the cross-painting rule is independent of lattice size and canvas size.

objects.why: Blocks are always 2x2 (hollow_rect 2x2 is solid) with a 1-cell gap; block size and gap are generator constants, not rule requirements.

placement.why: Offsets 0/1 shift the lattice so first-row/col blocks can be cut (incidental variety). row/col 1..5 exclude lattice index 0 (which can be cut to 1 row when offset=1, so excluding it keeps the marker block whole: rule-supported) but also exclude index 6, which is always fully visible (incidental).

density_colours.why: Lattice colour is fixed blue 1 and background 0 (incidental, no factory present); the marker colour is any non-1 colour (rule-supported distinctness).

rule_parameters.why: Only one marker and the row+column cross are the rule; no hidden parameter.

demonstration_context.why: Output is a deterministic function of the query; there is no direct factory; the certified evidence is a direct-source certificate, so no program consults demonstrations.

4f537728.proposal: High value per change: the whole native domain is 5*5*4 positions*offsets x 8 colours = 800 inputs (audit: 120 unique / 35 orbits). Parameterise lattice rows/cols (e.g. 3-9), block size (1-3) and gap (1-2), derive canvas from them (allow cropping on both sides), allow marker index 0..n-1 when the block is whole, and allow lattice colour as a parameter distinct from the marker. Recertify.
4f537728.uncertainties: Whether multiple markers (crossing crosses) are part of the original family is not shown by fixtures and is not proposed. Behaviour of cut marker blocks under the direct-source certificate is unknown.

placement.why: Panels at fixed offsets around the divider; every panel cell is sampled.

50c07299.mechanism: Orange (7) canvas of independent height/width 5..30 with a red (2) segment of length L on the anti-diagonal through the bottom-left corner (r + c = H-1), its lower-left cell at offset row along that diagonal; the output erases it and draws the next segment of length L+1 immediately up-right on the same diagonal.
50c07299.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs (3 train, 1 test), all 16x16, replayed exactly (validate lines 59-66; an explicit row keeps the 16x16 default, lines 42-43). (L, row) = (2,1), (1,0), (3,3) and (4,6) follow row = L(L-1)/2, the corner-anchored triangular series. Every canonical segment lies on the corner anti-diagonal.

dimensions.why: Height and width are drawn independently in 5..30 (34-35). The diagonal length is c = min(H, W) (36), and the canvas is grids(width, height, 7) (49) instead of the literal 16. Probe: 506 shapes in 1000. Certificate: 942/1000 unique, up from 56 (batch-C README).

objects.why: One diagonal segment is the rule's object. L is drawn 1..(c-1)//2 (39) so that L + (L+1) cells fit (guard 37). Probe max L is 14. This bound is rule-supported, not a literal.

placement.why: The offset along the diagonal is uniform, 0..c-1-2L (40), but the segment stays on the anti-diagonal through the bottom-left corner (51, 53). That matches every fixture, but the up-right continuation, and the factory's projection-based solver, would work on any parallel diagonal, so the offset limit is incidental. On non-square canvases the diagonal runs from the corner to an edge.

density_colours.why: Orange background and red segment are literals (49, 51, 53). The only colour variation is the factory/augmentation palette.

rule_parameters.why: Output length L+1 and adjacency (53) are the rule. Fixtures also fit 'next term of the corner-anchored series' (row = L(L-1)/2). The uniform row (40) drops that coupling. Both readings give the same output for any input, so labels are not ambiguous.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query. The unchanged factory (task_50c07299.py, a51474e) derives the direction from the D4 element and does not read demonstrations.

repair_delta.expanded: Independent 5..30 canvas, L up to 14, offset 0..c-1-2L. Exact default support is 31,304 inputs (probe enumeration of lines 34-40), up from 56.
repair_delta.retained: Corner anti-diagonal, up-right continuation of length L+1, orange/red literals, legacy 16x16 for explicit row.
repair_delta.unsolved: Diagonal offset away from the corner; literal colours.

50c07299.proposal: Medium. The tiny finite domain (56 inputs) is resolved: 31,304 inputs, 942/1000 unique in the certificate. Still open from the old proposal: a diagonal offset k (line r + c = k). 522fdd07.mechanism: 16x16 orange (7) canvas with 3-5 solid odd-sided squares (side 2L-1, L 1..5, distinct colours, 7 remapped to 0); each square shrinks by one ring around its centre, and single pixels (L=1) grow to a 9x9 square (L=5) around their cell.
522fdd07.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, 16x16. Pair 2: grey pixel at (5,10) becomes the 9x9 grey square rows 1-9 cols 5-13; pair 0 3x3 squares become single pixels. Pairs 0 and 1 contain no L=1 pixel, so they do not show the pixel->9x9 convention.

dimensions.why: Canvas and centre bounds use the literal 16; the shrink/grow rule needs a canvas of at least 9x9 for the pixel case, not 16x16.

objects.why: Square shape and centre-preserving shrink are rule; the L=1 -> L=5 wrap (line 58, side 9) is a fixed rule constant visible in fixtures, so L max 5 is rule-supported; 3-5 squares is incidental.

placement.why: Centres are chosen so input and output squares fit; non-overlap with a 1-cell margin is checked for both input footprints (line 40) and output footprints (line 44), keeping every square separable in both grids.

density_colours.why: Distinct colours per square (rule-supporting identification); background fixed to 7 and colour 0 used as a substitute for 7 (incidental literal).

rule_parameters.why: Shrink by 1 and wrap 1->5 are fixed constants of the rule.

demonstration_context.why: The pixel->9x9 convention is only learnable from pairs containing an L=1 square; with L uniform on 1..5 and 3-5 squares, P(no pixel) per pair is 0.8^n (0.51-0.33), so short episodes can lack it while the query needs it. No direct factory; certified evidence is a direct-source certificate.

522fdd07.proposal: Parameterise H,W (>= 9 each, e.g. 9-24) and scale square count to area; when assembling episodes, ensure at least one train pair contains an L=1 pixel if the query does (or bias L=1 probability). Recertify.
522fdd07.uncertainties: Episode-level coverage of the pixel convention was not measured; whether wrap target 5 should be 'largest seen square' rather than constant 5 is not decidable from fixtures.

52df9849.mechanism: Two layers of 1-3 objects each (rectangles, 45-degree diagonals for square boxes, or shaved staircases) on a 16x16 orange (7) canvas; the input draws layer 0 below layer 1, the output swaps the z-order. A layer solver (_visible_outputs, lines 80-113) enumerates every completion consistent with the visible input and only scenes with a unique answer equal to the output are kept.
52df9849.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 16x16. Pair 0: blue rectangle over yellow becomes yellow over blue; pair 2 has 5 bars (vertical over horizontal swapped); pair 3 has a slash diagonal (3) and a shaved staircase (8) plus red. Colours used exclude 7.

dimensions.why: Canvas grids(16, 16, 7) and size/position bounds 16/17 are literals; the solver (lines 80-113) is size-generic.

objects.why: 1-3 objects per layer and sizes 1..16 are incidental bounds; the shape vocabulary (rect, diagonal for squares, staircase shave) is constrained so _shape/_options can recover hidden parts, which is rule-supporting.

placement.why: Same-layer objects are 1-cell separated (line 175); every colour must be visible in both grids and partly obscured (lines 143, 152), and hidden input objects must keep over half their corners visible (157); together with the uniqueness check (223) these support unambiguous reconstruction.

density_colours.why: Colours are distinct across all objects and exclude background 7, since colour identifies an object; this is rule-supporting. Background 7 itself is a literal.

rule_parameters.why: The only rule is the z-order swap; no hidden parameter.

demonstration_context.why: Each kept input has exactly one solver-consistent output, so the query is determined without relying on demonstrations; factory does not reference demonstrations.

52df9849.proposal: Sample H,W (e.g. 8-24) and replace the 16/17 literals at lines 131, 173, 174; keep the solver-based uniqueness filter and bounded attempt loop (_MAX_ATTEMPTS). Expect acceptance to change with canvas size; remeasure. Recertify.
52df9849.uncertainties: Solver node budget (200000, line 88) behaviour on larger canvases is unmeasured; whether background colour 7 is part of the family's identity is unknown.

54db823b.mechanism: 4-6 non-overlapping green (3) rectangles (2-7 by 2-7, 1-cell separation) on a 15x15 black canvas, each speckled with maroon (9) pixels; pixel counts are sorted and distinct at the minimum, so box 0 has the unique fewest maroon pixels and is erased in the output.
54db823b.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, all 15x15, colours 0/3/9. In each pair the removed box has the fewest maroon pixels (e.g. pair 1 removes the 5x5 box at rows 1-5 cols 6-10 with one maroon pixel). Audit native: attempted 3, valid 1, 2 TimeoutErrors at the 2 s per-draw limit, so its fixed 15x15 and all ranges describe one scene. A fresh run here (probes/time_draws.py, seeds 0 and 1, 10 s limit) produced 70/70 valid draws, median 2-11 ms, max 3.4 s: the shortfall is a heavy rejection tail, not infeasibility.

dimensions.why: Canvas grids(15, 15) and the 15 in position bounds are literals; minimum-count deletion is size-independent.

objects.why: Box count 4-6 and size 2-7 are incidental; the 'fewer maroon than half the box' guard (line 46) supports reading boxes as green objects with maroon specks (rule-supported intent), but because sorted counts are assigned by index rather than by box area it rejects many feasible scenes.

placement.why: Non-overlap with spacing 1 (line 41) keeps boxes separable (rule-supported), but whole-scene rejection of 4-6 uniformly placed boxes in an unbounded while True loop (line 36) is the source of the heavy timing tail.

density_colours.why: Box colour 3, speck colour 9 and background 0 are literals in source and fixtures; no colour variation natively.

rule_parameters.why: Unique minimum count (line 43) makes the deleted box well defined; deleting index 0 (lines 61, 64) implements 'remove min'.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query with a unique minimum; factory does not reference demonstrations. The alternative reading 'remove smallest box by area' is not excluded by construction; whether fixtures/episodes disambiguate it was not checked.

54db823b.proposal: First make sampling well behaved: place boxes sequentially into free positions (like common.place_rectangles) instead of whole-scene rejection, assign pixel counts after choosing boxes with count <= area//2 per box, and bound the loop. Then sample H,W independently. Re-run the audit (the existing record has 1 valid draw) before judging diversity. Recertify.
54db823b.uncertainties: The timing evidence is 70 local draws, not the audit harness; whether some seeds take >10 s is unknown. Whether 'min maroon count' and 'min area' coincide often enough to confuse learners was not measured.

575b1a71.mechanism: 10x10 grey (5) canvas with black (0) holes in exactly four distinct columns (1-4 holes each); the output recolours each hole by the rank of its column among the four occupied columns, left to right, as colours 1,2,3,4.
575b1a71.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 10x10, input colours 0/5 only. Pair 0 columns 0,4,7,8 become 1,2,3,4; pair 2 adjacent columns 5,6 become 1,2, showing ranks rather than positions; every fixture has exactly four occupied columns.

dimensions.why: range(10) and grids(10, 10, 5) are literals; ranking occupied columns works for any H,W with at least four columns.

objects.why: Exactly four occupied columns (line 31) fixes the output palette to 1-4, as in all fixtures; 2-3 columns would still be well defined, but 5+ would need colour 5 which is the background, so <=4 is rule-supported and exactly 4 is incidental. Holes per column 1-4 is incidental.

placement.why: Hole rows and the four columns are uniform samples over the whole canvas; adjacency of columns is allowed, which is needed to show rank-not-position.

density_colours.why: Background 5 and hole colour 0 are literals; output colours 1-4 are the rule's rank code (rule-supported), and they must avoid the background, which the factory palette permutation preserves.

rule_parameters.why: sorted(cols) plus group+1 is the rank-to-colour rule; no hidden parameter.

demonstration_context.why: Rank colouring is a fixed convention visible in every pair; factory does not reference demonstrations.

575b1a71.proposal: Sample H,W independently (e.g. 5-20) and allow 2-4 occupied columns; keep the 1..k rank colours. Recertify. Variety is already high (128/128 unique audit inputs), so this is a dimension-only improvement.
575b1a71.uncertainties: Whether fewer than four columns is within the original family is not shown by fixtures (all have four).

5792cb4d.mechanism: A self-avoiding, non-self-touching 4-connected path of >= 7 cells with arbitrary per-cell colours (from 1,2,4,5,6,7,9) on an azure (8) 10x10 canvas; the output reverses the colour sequence along the path.
5792cb4d.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, 10x10. Pair 0 path 47165612 becomes 21656174; the test path has 28 cells and touches row 1 and column 8 but never the border rows/columns 0 and 9. Consecutive equal colours (e.g. 777, 666) occur.

dimensions.why: 10x10 literal canvas and start bounds 1..8; path reversal is size-independent.

objects.why: The look-ahead checks (lines 39-46) keep the path from touching itself, so its order and endpoints are recoverable: rule-supported. Minimum length 7 (line 55) and the 1/20 stop rate (line 48) are incidental length controls.

placement.why: Start in 1..8 and the r>1 / c<8 / r<8 / c>1 guards keep the whole path off the border ring, which also protects the r-2/c+2 index look-ups; the rule itself does not forbid border cells.

density_colours.why: Background 8 is literal; per-cell colours exclude 0, 3 and 8. Excluding the background is rule-supported; excluding 0 and 3 is incidental.

rule_parameters.why: Reversal along the path is the whole rule; reversal is symmetric in which end is called the start, so no hidden orientation parameter.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query; factory does not reference demonstrations.

5792cb4d.proposal: Sample H,W (e.g. 6-20), allow paths on the border by bounds-checking the look-ahead (use get_pixel) instead of excluding the border ring, and allow colours 0/3 when they differ from the background. Keep the non-touching constraint. Recertify.
5792cb4d.uncertainties: The bounded 256-try loop's failure rate on small canvases is unmeasured; whether paths touching the border change any learnt behaviour is unknown.

73182012.mechanism: An 8x8 fully D4-symmetric pattern, built from a transpose-symmetric 4x4 quadrant (3-6 colours on black), is placed at (brow,bcol) in 0..4 on a 12x12 black canvas; the 4x4 output is the top-left quadrant.
73182012.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 12x12 -> 4x4, placements (2,2), (0,0), (4,4), (0,2). Every output quadrant is transpose-symmetric (pair 0 row 0 = 0002 equals column 0), matching line 37.

dimensions.why: 12x12 canvas and the 4x4 quadrant (conway_sprite(4, 4, 10)) are literals; the quadrant-extraction rule works for any quadrant size and canvas. The factory already infers the quadrant size from demonstration outputs (_half_dims).

objects.why: A diagonally connected sprite mirrored into a transpose-symmetric quadrant (line 37) gives the D4-symmetric motif seen in all fixtures. conway_sprite never empties a whole row/column, so the 8x8 bounding box is always fully visible, which the factory relies on to locate the centre.

placement.why: brow,bcol in 0..4 are exactly the placements that fit an 8x8 motif in 12x12.

density_colours.why: 3-6 colours from 1-9 on black, drawn per cell (not all need appear); background 0 is literal.

rule_parameters.why: Natively the answer is always the top-left quadrant. Since the motif is D4-symmetric, which quadrant is the answer is a convention not determined by the input; the factory maps d4 to a corner (CORNER in build_program).

demonstration_context.why: Factory solve() reads the output size from demonstrations (_half_dims) and the corner convention is only visible through demonstration outputs (an episode-level d4 changes the corner). Any single pair suffices to show both, so episodes with >=1 train pair are adequate; this was reasoned from the factory source, not measured.

73182012.proposal: Sample quadrant size (e.g. 2-6) and canvas size independently (canvas >= 2*quadrant), with placements over the full range; keep transpose symmetry and the no-empty-row/column sprite. Recertify, including the factory's half-size inference.
73182012.uncertainties: Whether non-square quadrants are compatible with the transpose symmetry seen in fixtures: they are not, so quadrant must stay square. The factory's bounding-box fallback for motifs with empty outer lines is untested.

782b5218.mechanism: 10x10 grid with 50% noise in one colour X, crossed left to right by a red (2) gap-free line built by tiling a pattern of length 1-4 with a drift; the output keeps red, clears everything above the line to 0, and fills everything below with X.
782b5218.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 10x10. Canonical train[2] (identical to native validate()['train'][2]) has a red line that leaves through the bottom edge at column 8. Column 9 contains no red, and the output's column 9 is all zeros. Bottom exits and the cleared red-free column are therefore fixture-supported. probes/line_span_782b5218.py prints this counterexample. On 3000 native draws (seed 0) it finds 136 inputs (4.5%) with at least one red-free column; in all 136 those output columns are blank, exactly as in canonical train[2]. The factory's 4-connected top flood (edge 'top') agrees with the native output on all 3000. See erratum: the batch-2 text wrongly said every canonical line spans all 10 columns.

dimensions.why: 10x10 literals throughout; the clear-above/fill-below rule works on any canvas.

objects.why: A single gap-free red line (line 50 rejects vertical gaps) is rule-supported. The line may leave through the bottom edge, leaving red-free columns that the output clears to 0; canonical train[2] shows exactly this, so it is supported behaviour to preserve. The pattern length 1-4 and step rules (lines 37-42) are literal ranges and incidental.

placement.why: Start row 2..7 with a forced drift at the extremes (lines 44-46) is a literal range tied to the 10x10 canvas (incidental). Line 52 rejects only lines that leave the top. Bottom exits are allowed and fixture-supported (canonical train[2], column 9), so they must not be guarded away.

density_colours.why: Noise colour excludes red (rule-supported); noise density fixed at 0.5 (incidental, roughly matching fixtures); background 0 and line 2 are literals.

rule_parameters.why: Per column: keep 0 above, keep red, fill below with the noise hue: the rule itself.

demonstration_context.why: Natively the cleared side is always the top. The factory learns the cleared edge (top/right/bottom/left) by filtering against demonstrations and raises on ambiguity, so under an episode d4 the edge is a demonstration-conveyed convention; any one pair fixes it.

782b5218.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (e.g. 6-20), scaling the start-row range, and bound the while True loop at line 29. Keep bottom exits and red-free columns cleared to 0: they are fixture-supported, and a bottom-edge guard would narrow canonical support. No bottom guard is justified without new evidence. Re-audit and recertify.
782b5218.uncertainties: The 4.5% red-free rate comes from one local seed (3000 draws). Unknown: whether the original task also allows top exits, which line 52 forbids; no fixture shows one. Not measured: whether red-free columns change learnability.

erratum.summary: The batch-2 review called bottom exits a latent defect, rated the family high, and proposed a bottom-edge guard. That was wrong. 8ba14f53.mechanism: A 4x9 grid with two hollow boxes in distinct colours, side by side: widths 3..5, heights 3..4, gaps 0..1, optional notch (52-79, 31-39). The 3x3 output lists each box's hole count as a row-major run of its colour, one new row per box, left box first. Overflow is rejected (41-49).
8ba14f53.fixture_evidence: 7 canonical pairs (6 train, 1 test), 4x9 -> 3x3; holes per box (left first) [4,2], [3,2], [3,3], [1,1], [1,6], [2,3], [4,1] (probe), all within native box sizes. train[4] and test[0] show the left box first whatever the counts. Audit 128/128 unique, 76 orbits; certificate 970/1000.

dimensions.why: Literal 4x9 canvas (31), which only just fits two boxes (57, 59). The 3x3 output capacity is rule-derived, but it bounds hole counts, not the input canvas. Probe: native scenes padded with 0..4 blank rows/columns per side (77 canvas shapes) give the constructor's output in 400/400 factory runs.

objects.why: Two hollow boxes (one output row per box) with optional notch. The rule-derived limit is the sum of ceil(holes/3) over boxes <= 3, which admits a third box with <= 3 holes and taller interiors. The literal widths 3..5 and heights 3..4 (55, 58) are tighter than that.

placement.why: Gaps 0..1 and vertical offsets (56, 59) are bounded by the 4x9 canvas, not by the rule; margins preserve the mapping (probe 400/400).

density_colours.why: Two distinct box colours on 0, one per box, as in every fixture.

rule_parameters.why: Count holes, one row per box, left first.

demonstration_context.why: Left-first order is shown by canonical pairs where the left box has fewer holes. The factory fixes the reading direction per D4; no demonstrations read.

8ba14f53.proposal: Medium. Sample a larger independent canvas (e.g. H 4..30, W 9..30) with margins and box positions. Relax box sizes to the output-capacity bound (sum of ceil(holes/3) <= 3). Consider a third box only after checking the factory's ordering on three groups, which is untested. Recertify.
8ba14f53.uncertainties: Three-box scenes and taller interiors are not exercised by any fixture or probe. The factory's left-first ordering on padded scenes is probed only at d4 = 0.

8e301a54.mechanism: Three connected sprites (colours always 2, 5, 9) of at most 9 cells on a 10x10 orange (7) canvas; each sprite moves down by its own pixel count, and cells pushed past the bottom are dropped.
8e301a54.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 10x10, colours 2/5/7/9 only. Pair 3: the 3-cell grey column at rows 6-8 moves 3 down and only row 9 remains visible, so clipping at the bottom is fixture behaviour.

dimensions.why: 10x10 literal; the move-by-size rule is size-independent.

objects.why: Exactly three sprites with fixed colours (incidental); area <= 9 (line 34) bounds the drop distance relative to the canvas (incidental).

placement.why: Sprites must not share columns (overlaps_1d, line 36), so moving sprites can never collide; this is rule-supporting.

density_colours.why: Colours fixed to [2, 5, 9] (line 57) and background 7, exactly as in the fixtures; no native colour variation.

rule_parameters.why: Drop distance = pixel count; distinct deltas (line 53) make each displacement distinguishable.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query; factory does not reference demonstrations.

8e301a54.proposal: Sample H,W (e.g. 8-20), 2-4 sprites with distinct random colours, and an area cap scaled to the canvas height. Bound the while True at line 58. Recertify.
8e301a54.uncertainties: Line 52 requires every colour to stay visible after the drop; whether fully exiting sprites are allowed in the original is unknown.

9110e3c5.mechanism: Literal 7x7 canvas (35) filled from 49 colour draws (29). Each cell is 0 with p 1/2, otherwise the scene's key colour d in 1..3 (28) or a random_color 1..9 (30-33) with equal odds. The 3x3 output stamps a fixed glyph in 8 for the most frequent non-zero colour: 1 (44), 2 (45) or 3 (46). Any other dominant colour would give a blank output, which the sampler practically never draws. Ties go to the earlier colour after a stable sort (40-42).
9110e3c5.fixture_evidence: 9 canonical pairs (7 train, 2 test), all 7x7 -> 3x3, replayed by validate(). Dominant colours are 1,3,2,2,3,2,1,3,1, with counts 12-21 against runner-ups of 2-4 (probe), and every key appears in train. Native draws: dominant-minus-runner-up gap median 11 (min 0; 2/400 ties) against canonical gaps of 10-18 (probe). Audit: 128/128 unique, 4-10 colours, non-modal fraction 0.35-0.65.

dimensions.why: Literal 7x7 canvas (35) with exactly 49 draws (29). The rule only counts colours and the 3x3 output is the legend glyph, so nothing ties the input canvas to 7x7. The output size is intrinsic; the input size is not.

objects.why: There are no objects, only scattered pixels: one key colour per scene (rule-supported) plus random_color distractors (33), which may be the other keys.

placement.why: Every cell is sampled independently, and the rule ignores position.

density_colours.why: The background share is fixed at 1/2 and the key share at about 0.28 (30, 33). Canonical key counts (12-21 of 49) overlap native draws, but sparsity never varies. Keys are limited to 1..3 because the glyph table defines only those (44-46): this is an intrinsic legend.

rule_parameters.why: The most frequent non-zero colour selects a fixed glyph. Native ties (2/400) are broken by raster order (41-42); the direct_programs.py legend candidate raises on a tie instead.

demonstration_context.why: The glyph table is a demonstrated legend. The uncertified direct_programs.py candidate (lines 53-80) returns the output of a demonstration with the same key and raises if there is none, and build_million.py (lines 40, 706) requires the query key to be demonstrated. With three keys, an independent 3-demo episode misses the query key with probability (2/3)^3 = 0.30 (arithmetic, not measured).

9110e3c5.proposal: Medium, blocked on certification. First certify a native program (the legend candidate). Then sample an independent canvas (e.g. 3..30 per side) and a per-scene background share, keeping a unique key colour in 1..3 and the fixed glyphs. Recertify.
9110e3c5.uncertainties: direct-candidate-audit.json records passed=false ('Literal original grid in program'); whether that record describes the current legend candidate was not checked. Larger canvases, other sparsities and key-absent episodes were not probed.

917bccba.mechanism: 12x12: a hollow square (side 5-8) with full-length row and column lines of a second colour crossing inside it (offsets 2..size-3 from the box edge); the output moves the row line to the box's top edge row and the column line to the box's right edge column, with the box drawn over the lines.
917bccba.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 12x12, sizes 7, 6, 5, 8. In pair 0 the 8-coloured lines at row 6 and col 5 move to row 3 (box top) and col 8 (box right). The audit found 128 unique inputs but only 51 orbits.

dimensions.why: 12x12 literal and box bounds 11-size; the move-to-edge rule is size-independent.

objects.why: Always one square box; non-square boxes would leave the rule unchanged.

placement.why: Interior line offsets 2..size-3 keep the lines off and non-adjacent to the box edges (rule-supporting). The box never touches row/col 0 or 11 (incidental). Geometric domain is about 424 configurations (hand count from lines 35-38).

density_colours.why: Box and line colours are two distinct random colours from 1-9 (random_colors(2)) on a black background; distinctness keeps the box drawn over the moved lines readable, which is rule-supporting. Black background is a literal.

rule_parameters.why: Natively the destination is always top row plus right column; the factory d4 rotates this convention, and it is visible in any one pair.

demonstration_context.why: The convention is shown by every pair; factory does not reference demonstrations.

917bccba.proposal: Sample H,W (e.g. 8-24), rectangular boxes of any size >= 5 per side at any position, and line offsets in 2..side-3. This multiplies a ~424-configuration geometric domain (51 audit orbits). Recertify.
917bccba.uncertainties: The 424 count is a hand calculation from source; whether rectangular boxes are faithful is not shown by fixtures.

9356391f.mechanism: 16x16: a legend of 4-6 colours in row 0 above a grey (5) row 1, and one pixel of legend colour 0 below; the output draws concentric square rings around the pixel in legend order, and greys the legend swatch of any ring clipped by the drawing area (line 48).
9356391f.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, 16x16. Pair 0 legend 233408 with pixel at (11,5): ring 5 (colour 8) reaches row 16, so its swatch becomes 5 in the output (233405). Legend entries may repeat (3,3) and include 0 (an invisible ring).

dimensions.why: 16x16 literal and the clipping test bound 16; the ring rule is size-independent.

objects.why: One seed pixel and one ring per legend entry is the rule.

placement.why: Bounds let only the outermost ring be clipped, and only by one cell at the bottom, left or right (never the top). The clipping convention is rule-supported, but the narrow clipping cases are incidental.

density_colours.why: Legend colours are uniform 0-9 with first/last forced non-zero; repeats and 0 match the fixtures. Colour 5 (the grey of row 1 and of the clipped-swatch marker) can appear as a legend colour, so an unclipped swatch of 5 looks the same as a clipped one: deterministic but a semantic collision.

rule_parameters.why: Ring i takes colours[i]; a clipped ring greys its swatch. Both are fixed rule constants.

demonstration_context.why: The clipped-swatch convention is visible only in pairs where a ring is clipped (one of three canonical pairs); native episode coverage of clipping was not measured. Factory does not reference demonstrations.

9356391f.proposal: Sample H,W (e.g. 12-30) and the legend position, and exclude colour 5 from the legend (or make the clipped marker a separate role). Ensure episodes containing a clipped query also contain a clipped train pair. Recertify.
9356391f.uncertainties: How often native pairs clip a ring, and whether the original permits clipping at the top, are unknown.

94414823.mechanism: Black canvas (H 5..30, W 6..30 before transpose) with a grey (5) hollow square of even side 4..28 at a free position, and two marker pixels just outside its two top corners; the output splits the interior into four equal quadrants, giving each marker's colour to its nearest quadrant and the diagonally opposite one. 94414823.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs (3 train, 1 test), all 10x10 with a side-6 square at (2,2), replayed exactly. validate() (lines 88-95) passes explicit colours, so lines 56-60 keep the legacy geometry. objects.why: The square side is 2*randint(2, min(H-1, W-2)//2) (52): even, so quadrants are equal (guard 61, rule-supported), and up to 28. Probe sides: 4 (357), 6 (195), 8 (143), ..., 26 (1). Small squares dominate, but every even side that fits is reachable.

placement.why: Now free: brow 1..H-size and bcol 1..W-size-1 (53-54). Markers stay at the two adjacent outside corners of the top side (73-74); flip and transpose (79-82) give all four sides. Diagonal-corner markers are excluded, which is rule-supported because their quadrant claims would conflict.

density_colours.why: Two distinct non-grey marker colours (42) are rule-supported. The grey frame (72) and black background (68) are literals.

rule_parameters.why: The nearest-plus-opposite quadrant rule (75-78) is unchanged and now uses half = size // 2 for any even size.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query. There is no factory. The direct-source program (sha 617c4a43, current per probe) finds the frame as the largest object and assigns markers by side of the centre, reading only the query.

repair_delta.expanded: Canvas 5..30 x 6..30, even side 4..28, free position. Exact default support is 356,265 geometries x 56 ordered colour pairs x 4 transforms = 79,803,360 inputs (probe enumeration of lines 47-54), up from 224.
repair_delta.retained: Even interior split, adjacent-corner marker pair, grey frame and black background literals, legacy 10x10 for explicit colours.
repair_delta.unsolved: Literal frame/background colours only (diagonal markers are undefined by the rule).

95755ff2.mechanism: 11x11 fixed red (2) diamond outline with legend colours along row 0 (cols 6-10) and row 10 (cols 0-4) and sparse 'dust' pixels inside; each legend colour fills its column of the diamond interior, top legends downward and bottom legends upward, stopping at the first dust cell. 95755ff2.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 11x11. Pairs 1 and 2 have no dust; pair 0 dust (3) at (4,6),(4,7),(6,3) cuts fills. Legend entries repeat and include 0 (pair 2 tops 0,0,1,1,0).

dimensions.why: 11x11 canvas and the diamond of radius 5 are literals; the fill-until-blocked rule works for other diamond sizes.

objects.why: One diamond of fixed size; the geometry never changes apart from flop/transpose.

placement.why: Dust is placed only inside the diamond, never in the middle column (rule-supported: the middle column has no legend); the density of 1/20 is incidental. Only flop and transpose are sampled (no flip), giving 4 of the 8 D4 orientations natively.

density_colours.why: Legend colours come from the 9 colours other than the dust colour, with repeats (matching fixtures). The dust colour is random_color() 1-9 and can be 2, the diamond colour (P=1/9), making dust visually identical to the outline.

rule_parameters.why: Top legends fill down, bottom legends fill up, and fills stop at dust: fixed rule constants.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query; dust-stopping is visible whenever a pair has dust (most native pairs). Factory does not reference demonstrations.

95755ff2.proposal: Exclude colour 2 (the diamond) from the dust colour at line 55. Then parameterise the diamond radius (e.g. 3-7) with the canvas 2r+1 and legend lengths r, and add flip for the full D4. Recertify.
95755ff2.uncertainties: The 1/9 dust=red collision rate is computed from line 55, not measured; whether the original intends dust inside the diamond only is fixture-consistent but unproven.

97239e3d.mechanism: 17x17 black canvas with a 4x4 lattice of grey (8) 3x3 rings; for 1-2 colours, two corner pixels (optionally plus ring centres) mark a rectangle on the lattice gaps; the output draws the rectangle outline snapped to the gap lines and fills every enclosed ring centre with that colour.
97239e3d.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 17x17. Pair 0 has two colours (6, 1), each marked by two corner pixels; the test includes centre pixels for colour 2. Snapping (lines 75-78) maps pixels on ring edges back to gap lines.

dimensions.why: 17x17 canvas and the 4x4 lattice are literals; the rule works on any n x m lattice of period 4.

objects.why: 1-2 rectangles spanning 1-3 cells per axis are incidental to the 4x4 lattice; centre pixels with probability 1/8 are an incidental cue.

placement.why: Outlines may not cross another colour (lines 80-86), and rectangles sharing a ring centre are rejected (line 126, _shares_center) because the paint order would be hidden; both keep the label unique.

density_colours.why: Rectangle colours are distinct and exclude 8 (rule-supported); lattice 8 and background 0 are literals.

rule_parameters.why: Snap-to-gap and fill-enclosed-centres are the rule.

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query; factory does not reference demonstrations.

97239e3d.proposal: Parameterise lattice rows and columns (e.g. 2-7 each, canvas 4n+1) and allow up to 3 colours, keeping the shared-centre and crossing guards. Recertify.
97239e3d.uncertainties: Behaviour with many colours on small lattices (acceptance of the bounded 1000-try loop) is unmeasured.

981571dc.mechanism: A 30x30 crop of a 32x32 D4-symmetric mosaic (axes at 15.5, built from a transpose-symmetric 16x16 quadrant over 3-9 colours) with 1-6 rectangles erased to 0; the output restores every erased cell from a visible symmetric partner. Mask sets are accepted only if every erased cell has an unmasked partner inside the crop (_solvable).
981571dc.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, all 30x30, using colours 1-9 with 0 only in the erased patches. Pair 0 has six masks, including ones touching rows 27-29 and the right edge; its output restores them symmetrically.

dimensions.why: The 30-of-32 off-centre crop is the canonical structure and the module docstring calls the size intrinsic; but the symmetry-repair rule applies to any 2q mosaic cropped by 0-2 rows and columns, so the exact 30 is fixture-faithful rather than rule-required.

objects.why: Palette size 3-9, 1-6 masks of 1-10 by 1-10 that may overlap or adjoin.

placement.why: Masks may sit anywhere, provided every erased cell keeps a visible D4 partner (lines 76-83); this guard is what makes the label unique.

density_colours.why: Mosaic colours come from 1-9 and 0 is reserved for erasure, so erased cells are identifiable.

rule_parameters.why: The orbit map under the off-centre D4 group defines the repair.

demonstration_context.why: Each query is self-contained (solvable from its own visible partners); factory does not reference demonstrations.

981571dc.proposal: No patch is needed for diversity: 128/128 unique audit inputs with wide palette and mask variety. An optional extension samples the latent half-size (e.g. 8-16) and crop (0-2) as a separately certified variant; it is not required for faithfulness.
981571dc.uncertainties: Whether non-30 sizes belong to the original family is unknown (all fixtures are 30x30); the configured/legacy extension path (legacy_extension_available=true) was not reviewed here.

996ec1f3.mechanism: A 19x19 grid of uniform noise from colours 1-9 (line 34, random_color) is split into quadrants by a full plus of colours[4] at row prow and column pcol, each drawn from 6-12 (line 32). Each quadrant is then overwritten by a solid rectangle of a distinct colour, inset by one noise cell from the border and from the plus (lines 41-44). The output is a 3x3 summary: the four quadrant colours in the corners and the plus colour in the cross (lines 45-49).
996ec1f3.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, all 19x19 -> 3x3. Pair 0: plus colour 3 at row 11, col 8; blocks 1/9/8/2; output 139/333/832. Noise never uses 0. probes/fixture_stats_batch3.py counts zeros per input as [0, 0, 37, 72]: pair 2's 37 zeros are its 0-coloured plus (19+19-1), and the test's 72 are its 0-coloured bottom-left block. This matches random_color's 1-9 range. Noise reuses role colours (pair 0, row 10 contains 3, the plus colour), as native noise can. Audit native: 128/128 valid and unique, fixed 19x19. Native draws never contain such a tie, so the centre tie convention is canonical-only. Audit native: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: The 10x10 canvas and the loop bounds of 10 are literals; the longest-diagonal rule applies on any rectangle.

objects.why: One connected black region is rule-supported (line 39). The edge-run lengths come from a fixed 1-4 histogram, which is incidental.

placement.why: Every row and column gets an edge run on all four sides. This keeps the shape a grey-framed blob: a fixture-faithful but fixed construction.

density_colours.why: Grey on black is fixed. Black density follows the fixed run-length histogram (non-modal fraction 0.26-0.49).

rule_parameters.why: The native rule is the longest diagonal by total black count (line 47). The tie rule (lines 53-57) appears only in canonical pair 1, never natively. Construction also does not separate the full-count reading from a contiguous-run reading.

demonstration_context.why: The factory solve enumerates 10 hypotheses: full diagonal or contiguous run, crossed with five tie criteria. It keeps those that uniquely reproduce every demonstration and raises unless the survivors agree on the query. The certificate records 113 context retries, so the rule's identity is chosen from context.

aa300dc3.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (8-14) with run lengths scaled. Optionally admit tie scenes resolved by the centre convention, so that native episodes can show the canonical tie-break. Recertify against the factory's hypothesis class.
aa300dc3.uncertainties: Unknown: whether the original rule counts contiguous runs or the whole diagonal, and how ties break beyond the single canonical example. Not measured here: how often native contexts separate the run reading from the full-count reading.

aaecdb9a.mechanism: This is a hand-written constructor (d71ead8). On a 10x10 orange-7 canvas (SIZE, line 28), 2-5 legend colours from {5,2,8,9,6} place 1..height objects each. One colour reaches height 2-6 (lines 113-118). Objects are drawn from 31 shape templates, including blobs and lines up to 9 (lines 51-87), and same-colour objects are kept 8-separated (lines 97-108). The output is an H x 5 bottom-anchored bar chart of object counts in fixed legend slots (lines 176-184).
aaecdb9a.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 10x10. Outputs are 2x5, 3x5, 5x5 and 6x5. Different-colour objects touch in train[2] (8 next to 9 and 7), which is allowed. The audit is stale, recorded on an older source (fb0c522e is the current hash). native-certificates/aaecdb9a.json: 1000 fresh pairs, constructor current. verified_rules.py replaces the archived modal-colour verifier with legend_object_chart, because dense scenes can make a legend colour modal. aaecdb9a-dense-counterexample.json records one such scene. That is a verifier mismatch, not an invalid scene.

dimensions.why: The canvas is a literal SIZE = 10 (incidental). The output is height = max count by 5 legend slots, which the rule requires.

objects.why: There is wide shape variety (31 templates plus blobs). The height of 2-6 and 2-5 colours are literals bounded by the canvas and legend; height 1 is never drawn.

placement.why: Same-colour objects are 8-separated so counts are unambiguous. Different colours may touch, as in canonical train[2].

density_colours.why: Background 7 and the five legend colours are fixed by the rule's legend. Dense scenes are valid and covered by the verifier override.

rule_parameters.why: Each legend colour's 8-connected objects are counted into a bottom-anchored bar in that colour's slot.

demonstration_context.why: The factory uses fixed SLOTS per d4 and never reads demonstrations. The slot order is a constant convention shown by every pair.

aaecdb9a.proposal: Medium. Replace SIZE with sampled H and W (6-30) and scale the height cap with area. Keep 8-separation and the legend. Recertify using the existing legend_object_chart verifier. Then rerun the stale audit.
aaecdb9a.uncertainties: Whether 1-row outputs (height 1) are within the original rule.

aaef0977.mechanism: An 8x8 orange (7) grid holding one seed pixel at a random position. The seed's colour is one of nine colours in a fixed cycle (lines 29-35). Each output cell is the cycle colour at the seed's index plus that cell's Manhattan distance from the seed, mod 9 (lines 36-38).
aaef0977.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, 8x8, with seeds 3 at (0,6), 5 at (5,2) and 0 at (2,1). Outputs show the cycle 0,5,2,8,9,6,1,3,4 radiating in Manhattan rings. Audit native: 118 of 128 inputs unique but only 10 orbits, the D4 position classes of a single pixel on an 8x8 board. The whole native domain is 64 positions x 9 seed colours = 576 inputs; the certificate saw 474 unique in 1000 draws.

dimensions.why: The 8x8 canvas is a literal. The ring rule is defined on any HxW, and the factory reads H and W from the grid.

objects.why: A single seed pixel is the rule's whole input.

placement.why: The seed may sit anywhere on the board, including corners and edges.

density_colours.why: The 9-colour cycle order is the rule. The factory remaps it through the palette, keeping the order.

rule_parameters.why: colour = cycle[(index + |dr| + |dc|) mod 9], with no free parameter beyond seed position and colour.

demonstration_context.why: The cycle must be learned from demonstration outputs. Any output reaching distance 8 or more shows the whole cycle, so one 8x8 pair suffices. The factory hardcodes the cycle through the palette and does not read demonstrations.

aaef0977.proposal: High: the domain is only 576 inputs. Sample H and W independently (e.g. 5-16), with a guard that H+W >= 10 so outputs still show all nine cycle colours. Recertify.
aaef0977.uncertainties: Untested: on small canvases, demonstrations might not reveal the whole cycle. Unknown: whether non-square canvases fit the original task.

ad38a9d0.mechanism: A 9x9 orange (7) board holding 6-8 grey (6) shapes. There are six fixed silhouettes (I3, plus, L-tromino, 2x3 block, S-tetromino, domino); each scene has one of each plus 0-2 repeats (lines 128-132). Shapes are packed with edge clearance; diagonal contact is allowed (_sample_positions, lines 20-61; adjacency checks, lines 115-123). The output recolours each grey shape by a fixed silhouette-to-colour map onto 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 (lines 84-114).
ad38a9d0.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, 9x9, colours 6/7. Pair 0 has 8 shapes (all six plus repeats of 4 and 2), pair 1 exactly six, and the test seven. Every fixture shows all six silhouettes in a fixed orientation; e.g. the 4-shape is always (0,0),(0,1),(1,1). Audit native: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: The 9x9 board is a literal, also used for the packer's bounds.

objects.why: Every input contains all six silhouettes, so a single demonstration reveals the whole map. The 0-2 extras are incidental and could scale with area.

placement.why: Shapes never share an edge, so each is a separate 4-connected component (rule-supported). Diagonal contact is allowed, as in the fixtures.

density_colours.why: Grey-on-orange input and the fixed map to six output colours are the rule's roles. The factory palette remaps them.

rule_parameters.why: The silhouette-to-colour map is fixed and orientation-specific. D4 augmentation rotates the whole episode consistently, so the fixed orientation is part of the rule here.

demonstration_context.why: The map is learnable from any one demonstration because all six shapes are always present. The factory hardcodes the map through the palette and does not read demonstrations.

ad38a9d0.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (8-14) and scale the extra-shape count with area. Keep all six silhouettes present and the edge clearance. The packer is already bounded (max_nodes 4096, 256 tries, raises on failure). Recertify.
ad38a9d0.uncertainties: Unknown: whether the original task ever omits a silhouette (all fixtures include all six). Not measured: packer success rates on other canvases.

af24b4cc.mechanism: A 9x10 black canvas with a 2x3 array of 3x2 tiles at rows 1-3/5-7 and cols 1-2/4-5/7-8 (lines 28-37). Each tile mixes two colours from 1-9, with the minority colour appearing 1-2 times (line 34). The 4x5 output is a black border around the 2x3 grid of tile majorities (lines 43-50).
af24b4cc.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 9x10 -> 4x5. Every tile is 3x2 with two colours and a clear majority: e.g. pair 0's tile 11/11/33 gives 1, and its tile 44/44/48 gives 4. No tile uses 0. Audit native: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: The canvas, tile array and tile size are all literals. The reference program derives the tile rows and columns from runs of non-background cells and sizes its output from their counts.

objects.why: Six tiles of exactly two colours, each with a unique majority (rule-supported). The 2x3 array and 3x2 tile size are incidental.

placement.why: The fixed lattice with one-cell gaps keeps tiles separable by background runs, as the reference program needs (rule-supported). That the positions never vary is incidental.

density_colours.why: Two distinct non-zero colours per tile, with the majority on 4-5 of 6 cells: the majority is unique by construction.

rule_parameters.why: Each output cell is its tile's majority colour.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained. The direct_certificate reference transform(grid) uses only the query grid.

af24b4cc.proposal: Medium: sample tile-array rows 1-4 and columns 2-5, tile size 2-4 per axis, and 2-3 colours per tile with a strict majority. The canvas follows from these. Recertify the reference program.
af24b4cc.uncertainties: Unknown: whether the original task varies the tile array (all fixtures use 2x3) and whether three-colour tiles fit it.

afe3afe9.mechanism: A 30x30 black canvas with a blue (1) marker line along one edge (line 49). Beside it is a 7x7 lattice of hollow 3x3 squares at pitch 4 (lines 50-55). The left three lattice columns hold two colour groups (rows 0-2 and 4-6, line 37); the right three hold azure (8) squares; the centre column is empty. The output is the 7x6 lattice with each row's squares packed toward the azure side (lines 56-63). Flip, flop and transpose are each applied independently, to input and output together (lines 42-44, 64-66).
afe3afe9.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 30x30, with output shapes 7x6, 6x7, 7x6 and 6x7. Orientation therefore varies within the episode, as it does natively. Pair 0 uses colours 2 and 3 on the left and 8 on the right, and its output rows are right-packed (222888, 000028, ...). Audit native: 128/128 unique, outputs 6x7 or 7x6.

dimensions.why: 30x30 is the 7-row lattice at pitch 4 plus margin and the marker row, so the size is tied to the lattice. But the 7x7 lattice is itself fixed (incidental), and the factory raises on any other lattice size.

objects.why: Each lattice row has 1-3 squares per side (randint(1,3)). The two left colour groups follow a fixture-faithful layout.

placement.why: Orientation is random per pair. The flop offset (line 55) keeps the lattice aligned, so orientation varies as in the fixtures.

density_colours.why: Two foreground colours come from 1-9 excluding 1 and 8. Azure and blue are fixed roles, which the factory receives as palette[1] and palette[8].

rule_parameters.why: Native packs toward the azure side. The certificate notes that canonical pairs also fit a 'clockwise relative to the marker' reading; odd-handed native cases separate the two.

demonstration_context.why: The factory keeps three hypotheses (toward azure, clockwise, counter-clockwise), filters them on the demonstrations, and raises if they disagree on the query. The certificate records 39 context retries.

afe3afe9.proposal: Low/medium: vary the lattice height (5-7) and per-side width (2-4), with the canvas following. This needs a matching factory change, because the factory hardcodes a 7x7 lattice. Orientation and colour variety are already good. Recertify.
afe3afe9.uncertainties: Unknown: whether lattice sizes other than 7x7 belong to the original task (all fixtures use 7x7), and what context-retry rates a different geometry would need.

b0722778.mechanism: A 9-wide canvas with 3n-1 rows (73-74), where n = 3..4 bands (31). Each band holds a 2x2 block A (columns 0-1), its transform (columns 3-4) and a block B (columns 7-8). The transforms are R, L or O, and optionally one band uses the global colour map C (32-37, 55-62). The 2-wide output applies each band's transform to B (64-71, 89-93). Block colourings are two-colour stripes for R/L and one odd cell for O (40-54).
b0722778.fixture_evidence: 3 pairs (2 train, 1 test) with bands ORC, CRLO and ORL. Audit: 128/128 unique. The gate analogy_priority_evidence is dispatched from colour_evidence.py (347-351).

dimensions.why: Height follows the band count (rule-tied). The 9-wide layout is constant across fixtures.

objects.why: 3..4 bands; the bound 3n-1 <= 30 allows n <= 10.

placement.why: The three-block layout per band is the task.

density_colours.why: Block colourings are restricted per transform (stripes or one odd cell), which keeps transforms identifiable but narrows content.

rule_parameters.why: Apply the transform that the band itself shows (A to its neighbour block: R, L, O or colour map C) to block B.

demonstration_context.why: Transform priority is learnt per episode by analogy_priority_evidence, which compares all 8! orderings of D4 operations (colour_evidence.py 347-351).

b0722778.proposal: Medium. Sample n in 2..10 bands and keep the layout; recertify with the gate.
b0722778.uncertainties: Whether richer block colourings belong to the task. Gate retry rates for more bands were not measured.

b1fc8b8e.mechanism: Literal 6x6 canvas (47). It holds four non-overlapping pieces, either all 2x2 squares or all L-trominoes (a 2x2 square missing its top-left cell) (28, 30-39), with top-left corners in 0..4 (31-32). L scenes also require some piece's missing corner to be covered by another piece (40-43). The output is a fixed 5x5 motif of four 2x2 quadrants (50-54); when the input has 12 cells, the quadrant corners are cleared (53).
b1fc8b8e.fixture_evidence: 7 pairs (5 train, 2 test), 6x6 -> 5x5, with 16,16,12,12,12,12,16 cells. In every pair the bottom row is blank; 6 of 7 inputs are one 4-connected blob (probe). The exact native domain is 3145 inputs: 1158 L scenes and 1987 square scenes (probe). Native draws form one 4-connected blob in 108/400 (probe). Audit: 125/128 unique; certificate: 847/1000.

dimensions.why: The 5x5 output is a fixed legend motif (intrinsic). The 6x6 input canvas is a literal (47), and the factory only counts non-background cells, so the input canvas is incidental.

objects.why: Four pieces of one type is what the output distinguishes, and every fixture has 12 or 16 cells. The piece count is fixture-supported, but it is also what lets the factory's cell-count threshold stand in for piece shape.

placement.why: Pieces are free within 0..4 apart from non-overlap. Canonical inputs are interlocked blobs (6/7 4-connected, bottom row blank in 7/7), while native draws are connected in 108/400. Scattering widens support, but it departs from the canonical look; the rule (a cell count) does not require connectivity.

density_colours.why: One ink colour 8 on 0, with fixed roles as in every fixture.

rule_parameters.why: The 12-vs-16 split (53) is the piece-type signal; the factory thresholds at 14. Within this domain, reading it as arm thickness or as cell count gives the same answer.

demonstration_context.why: Query-only factory; both motifs appear in canonical train.

b1fc8b8e.proposal: Medium. Sample a larger independent canvas (e.g. 6..15 per side) and keep four pieces. Add an interlocked-blob layout mode matching the fixtures. Vary piece counts only after replacing the count threshold with a shape test. Recertify.
b1fc8b8e.uncertainties: The original discriminating feature (arm thickness or cell count) is unknown; varied piece counts would separate the two and are untested. The factory on larger canvases was not probed.

b2bc3ffd.mechanism: An 8x8 orange (7) canvas with an azure (8) floor in row 7. On the floor sit objects: bars or corner-trimmed blocks 1-6 wide and 1-3 tall, each a distinct colour from 1-9 excluding 7 and 8, separated by 1-2 empty columns (lines 28-54). In the output each object rises by its own cell count (lines 59-69).
b2bc3ffd.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 8x8. In pair 0 the maroon object (4 cells) rises 4 rows and the red bar (3 cells) rises 3. In pair 3 a 6-wide grey bar rises 6 to row 0. Every object stands on the floor and has its own colour. Audit native: 127 of 128 unique, 98 orbits; the certificate counted 940 unique in 1000.

dimensions.why: The 8x8 literal is tied to lift headroom: the largest object (6 cells, or 3 tall plus a lift of 3) still fits in 7 rows. A larger canvas needs these caps to scale with it.

objects.why: Width and height histograms plus corner trimming give simple bars and steps (incidental). One colour per object (line 36) is rule-supported, because the lift counts cells by colour (lines 59-65).

placement.why: Objects are packed left to right with gaps of 1-2 on a bottom floor. This is fixture-faithful but a fixed scan order.

density_colours.why: Distinct object colours on an orange background with an azure floor are rule roles, remapped by the factory palette.

rule_parameters.why: Each object's lift equals its total cell count.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained. The factory maps the lift direction from d4 and does not read demonstrations.

b2bc3ffd.proposal: Medium: sample H (8-14) and W (6-14), bounding object size so that cells plus height stays at most H-1. This widens the domain beyond about 1000 inputs. Recertify.
b2bc3ffd.uncertainties: Unknown: whether objects in the original task are always floor-anchored bars (the fixtures agree). The domain size is estimated from certificate and audit uniqueness, not enumerated.

b4a43f3b.mechanism: 13x6 input (44): a 3x3 motif upscaled 2x on top (47-49), a grey divider row 6 (45-46) and a 6x6 placement map below (50-53). The motif is a diagonally connected 3x3 sprite coloured from {1,2,3,6} (29-33). The map is three axis-aligned segments of colour 2 with lengths 1..6 (35-41). The 18x18 output stamps the motif at each map cell (54-56).
b4a43f3b.fixture_evidence: 5 pairs (4 train, 1 test), all 13x6 -> 18x18. Axis segments needed per canonical map: 2, 4, 2, 3, 3 (probe). Train[1]'s map (a 2x2 block plus two diagonal cells) needs four segments, so native draws cannot produce it. Motif colours in the fixtures are 1, 2, 3 and 6. Audit: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: Literal 13x6 input and 6x6 map. The rule bound is 3P, 3Q <= 30 (maps up to 10x10 with the 3x3 motif). The factory reads the map at any size with MOTIF_N = 3, but larger maps were not probed.

objects.why: The map is exactly three axis-aligned segments (35-41). That excludes canonical train[1], which needs four (probe). The rule stamps any binary map.

placement.why: Segment positions are free on the 6x6 map; the motif region and divider are fixed, as in every fixture.

density_colours.why: Motif colours come from the literal set {1,2,3,6} (33), matching the fixtures; the map colour 2 is literal. A motif cell may share the map colour, as canonical train[0] and train[3] show.

rule_parameters.why: Stamp the 3x3 motif at every non-background map cell; no free parameter beyond the motif and the map.

demonstration_context.why: The factory's solve() reads only the query grid, never the demonstrations, and nothing in the rule depends on episode context.

b4a43f3b.proposal: High: a canonical input is unreachable. Replace the three-segment map with a general non-empty binary map, or 1..6 segments plus free cells, on P x Q up to 10 x 10, so that train[1] is reachable. Widen motif colours to 1..9 except the divider. Probe the factory on non-6x6 maps, then recertify.
b4a43f3b.uncertainties: The factory on maps other than 6x6 was not run. It derives the motif step as region//3, and a motif region narrower than a wider map is untested.

b7fb29bc.mechanism: A fixed 9x9 green (3) frame at rows 2-10 and cols 3-11 on a 15x15 black canvas, with one green seed inside its 7x7 interior (lines 29-36, 41). The output colours each interior cell red (2) or yellow (4) by the parity of its Chebyshev distance from the seed (lines 37-40).
b7fb29bc.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 15x15, colours 0/3. The frame is identical in every pair, and the seeds sit at interior (5,1), (3,3), (0,5) and (2,0). Audit native: 46 unique inputs, 26 orbits. The certificate records an exhaustive finite domain of the 49 seed positions.

dimensions.why: Canvas size, frame position and frame size are literals. The factory finds the largest green component and works inside it.

objects.why: One frame of fixed size; the only variation is the seed position.

placement.why: The seed may be anywhere in the interior (rule-supported), but the frame never moves (incidental).

density_colours.why: The green frame, red/yellow rings and black background are fixed; the palette remaps them only at episode level.

rule_parameters.why: Parity of Chebyshev distance from the seed: even distances red, odd yellow.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained; the factory does not read demonstrations.

b7fb29bc.proposal: High: the domain is only 49 inputs. Randomise frame height and width (e.g. 5-13 per side, rectangular), frame position and canvas size; the rule and factory already handle any frame. Recertify; the finite-domain exemption would then lapse.
b7fb29bc.uncertainties: Unknown: whether non-square frames fit the original task (all fixtures share one 9x9 frame).

b9630600.mechanism: 6-8 hollow green (3) rectangles, 3-12 per side, on a 30x30 black canvas. They grow outward from a seed box: each new neighbour is centred on its parent's side with matching parity (lines 158-183). The output joins nested-span neighbours with two-line 'pipes' along a minimum spanning tree of gap lengths, opening the walls where pipes meet (lines 107-151). A scene is accepted only if all boxes merge with at least 5 merges (lines 152-153) and the MST over visible pipe candidates is unique (_visibly_determined, lines 81-85, 185).
b9630600.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 30x30, colours 0/3, with 7, 6, 7 and 8 boxes. Pair 0's output shows pipes; e.g. rows 5-6 join the box at cols 2-7 to the box at cols 11-14 through opened walls. Audit native: 128/128 unique, 0.34 s.

dimensions.why: 30 is a literal in the canvas and in the bounds; the pipe rule works at any size.

objects.why: 6-8 boxes with at least 5 merges match the fixture counts. Both bounds follow from the 30x30 canvas.

placement.why: Children are centred with matching parity (lines 172-182). The ill-defined guards (lines 112 and 118) require centred nesting, so each pipe lies on symmetric interior lines. The visible-uniqueness gate (line 185) makes the answer determinable from the input.

density_colours.why: Green on black is fixed; the factory palette remaps it.

rule_parameters.why: Pipes are added in increasing gap order, skipping already-merged groups (Kruskal's algorithm), and the resulting tree is unique.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained per query. The factory raises on a non-unique tree and does not read demonstrations.

b9630600.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (20-30) and use 4-8 boxes scaled to area. The sampler is already bounded (_MAX_SCENES). Recertify.
b9630600.uncertainties: Not measured: acceptance rates on smaller canvases. Unknown: whether fewer than 6 boxes fit the original task.

bb52a14b.mechanism: A 22x22 grid of 20% blue/azure (1/8) noise (line 76). It holds 2-3 copies of a 3x3 pattern of 1, 8 and 0; in copy 0 the pattern's zero cells are yellow (4) (lines 59-71, 81). The output stamps the full yellow-holed pattern on every other place where the non-yellow cells match (lines 34-55). A scene is rejected if any match has a non-zero cell at a yellow position (lines 43, 46), lies on the border (line 47), or overlaps another match (line 50).
bb52a14b.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 22x22, colours 0/1/4/8, with 2-3 pattern copies each (pair 0: yellow copy at (12,4), stamps at (2,10) and (12,18)). Audit native: only 70 valid of 72 attempted, with 2 TimeoutErrors. probes/time_draws.py (seeds 0 and 1, 5 s limit) gave 46/48 and 45/48 valid draws. Successful draws had a median of 1.1 ms and a maximum of 4 ms, and the 5 failures all hit the limit: a bimodal pattern, not a heavy tail. probes/stuck_scenes_bb52a14b.py (300 scenes, 200 noise redraws each, seed 0) found 10/300 scenes (3.3%) that never accept, and all 10 are rejected even with zero noise. Every printed stuck example has a box centred at row or column 1 or 20, i.e. touching the border.

dimensions.why: 22 is a literal throughout. The fixed 22x22 audit signal is real (it comes from the source), not a sampling artefact, but the audit's other ranges describe only 70 scenes.

objects.why: 2-3 copies of one pattern, a cross or X template with one extra zero (fixture-faithful). The copy count is incidental.

placement.why: The 7x7 non-overlap spacing (line 50) and the no-border-match rule (line 47) are rule-supported. But the copy positions and pattern are drawn once, outside the noise loop (lines 59-71), so a rejection caused by the copies alone can never clear: the loop at line 72 then never ends.

density_colours.why: Noise density is fixed at 1/5 and noise colours at 1/8, with yellow as the marker. The palette remaps the colours only at episode level.

rule_parameters.why: Match on the non-yellow cells, require 0 or 4 at the yellow cells, then stamp the yellow-holed pattern.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained per query; the factory does not read demonstrations.

bb52a14b.proposal: High. Fix sampling first: about 3% of native scenes hang forever at line 72. Either move the pattern and copy draws (lines 59-71) inside a bounded retry loop, or reject copy placements whose partial border matches trip lines 41 and 47. Re-run the audit (the existing record has 70 valid draws), then sample H, W and noise density. Recertify.
bb52a14b.uncertainties: The border-partial-match explanation is inferred from the stuck examples (each has a copy at an edge) and from line 41 skipping out-of-bounds cells before line 47 rejects; the failing match was not traced per example. The 3.3% rate comes from one seeded run of 300 scenes.

bbb1b8b6.mechanism: Literal 4x9 canvas (32, 48). The left 4x4 pattern in colour 1 has 4..12 cells (33-35), column 4 is a grey divider (41), and the right 4x4 shape is one colour other than 1 or 5 (31). That shape is the exact complement (36) or, with p 1/2, a random 4..12-cell mask (37-40). The output overlays the two panels if the right shape exactly fills the left holes (51-57), and is the left panel otherwise.
bbb1b8b6.fixture_evidence: 9 pairs (7 train, 2 test), 4x9 -> 4x4: 5 exact and 4 non-exact. The non-exact distractors are near misses, with (holes, cells) = (4,4), (9,8), (6,5), (8,6), and are coherent shapes; train[1] puts the hole-sized 2x2 block in the wrong place. Native draws: 183/400 non-exact, of which 33 have as many cells as holes (probe), and all are random masks. Probe: the factory matches an independent reference on 400/400 inputs over 241 shapes (panels up to 30 x 14, including near misses).

dimensions.why: Literal 4x4 panels. The factory splits at any divider with equal panels (probe 400/400); the bound is 2W+1 <= 30.

objects.why: The left pattern is any 4..12-cell mask. The right shape is the complement or random noise, so the coherent shapes of the fixtures are not sampled.

placement.why: The panels are aligned cell by cell by construction, and that alignment is the rule.

density_colours.why: Colours 1 and 5 are literal roles and the right colour is random (31). Distractors are noise: canonical-style near misses (equal count or one cell off) are uncommon natively (33/183 equal count).

rule_parameters.why: Overlay only on an exact positional complement.

demonstration_context.why: Readings such as 'counts match' or 'shape fits somewhere' would differ from the exact positional complement. Canonical train[1] separates them (4 holes, 4 cells, wrong place, no overlay), but native noise distractors seldom do. The factory reads no demonstrations, and episode-level ambiguity was not measured.

bbb1b8b6.proposal: Medium. Sample panel H x W (2..30 x 2..14). Draw some distractors as near misses (a complement with one or two cells moved, or the hole shape shifted) alongside random ones. Recertify.
bbb1b8b6.uncertainties: Episode-level hypothesis ambiguity was not measured. Whether near-miss distractors are part of the task is inferred from four canonical pairs.

dimensions.why: Height is incidental: the factory copies any H. Width is ambiguous. Every fixture is 4 wide with five copies, so 'five copies' and 'W+1 copies' fit equally well; the factory fixes five. The bound is 5W <= 30.

objects.why: There are no objects; every 4x4 arrangement of the chosen colours is reachable.

placement.why: The whole tile is copied; nothing depends on position.

density_colours.why: 2..3 colours with no 0, matching the fixtures. The rule never reads colours, so the count limit is incidental but harmless.

rule_parameters.why: O,M,O,M,O along the width in every fixture. The copy count against width is undetermined (see dimensions).

demonstration_context.why: The factory's solve() reads only the query grid, never the demonstrations, and nothing in the rule depends on episode context.

bc4146bd.proposal: Medium. Sample H freely now (1..30). Vary W only after choosing a copy-count reading (five fixed or W+1). Recertify.
