bd283c4a.mechanism: A 10x10 grid fully filled with four colours from 1-9, drawn with fixed weights 10/6/3/1 out of 20 (lines 28-30). The output stacks colours by descending count, filling column by column from the bottom-left, upward then rightward (lines 36-41). Tied counts keep dict insertion order, i.e. first appearance in row-major order (line 36, with the stable sort at line 38).
bd283c4a.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, 10x10, using 3-4 colours each. Pair 0 (colours 4, 9, 5, 8) fills 4s in the left columns and ends with 8s at the top right. Audit native: 128/128 unique, always 4 colours. probes/fixture_stats_batch3.py found tied counts in 38/2000 native inputs (1.9%, seed 0); in those, the first-appearance tie-break decides the output. The factory reproduces that convention through a d4-mapped scan.

dimensions.why: The 10x10 literal is also hardcoded in the fill index (line 40).

objects.why: Always 4 colours; the rarest is absent in only about 0.6% of draws. 3-6 colours would not change the rule.

placement.why: Every one of the 100 cells is drawn independently from the weighted list (line 30), so colour positions are unconstrained.

density_colours.why: The fixed 10/6/3/1 weights pin the colour-count profile, while the fixtures show varied profiles.

rule_parameters.why: The descending-count fill is the rule. The first-appearance tie-break is an implementation artefact that demonstrations rarely show (1.9% of pairs).

demonstration_context.why: Deterministic per query. The factory hardcodes the tie convention and does not read demonstrations, but a learner sees the convention only in the rare tied pairs.

bd283c4a.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (6-14) and 2-6 colours with random weights. Either reject tied counts (about 2% cost) or document the tie-break as a convention. Recertify.
bd283c4a.uncertainties: The 1.9% tie rate comes from one seeded run of 2000. Whether the original task ever has ties is unknown.

be03b35f.mechanism: Literal 5x5 canvas (32). The TL, TR and BL 2x2 quadrants hold successive clockwise rotations of a binary 2x2 pattern in colour 1 (33-36), and BR is a red 2x2 (37). The output is the next rotation (33-36).
be03b35f.fixture_evidence: 4 pairs (3 train, 1 test), 5x5 -> 2x2. The native domain is exactly 14 inputs, the non-constant binary patterns (29-30). The probe and the certificate's exhaustive finite_default_domain both count 14, and native draws reach all 14 in 400. Probe: the factory matches an independent reference (which replays all 4 pairs) on 385/385 scenes with k x k quadrants (k 2..9, gap 1..3).

dimensions.why: Literal 5x5 canvas with 2x2 quadrants. The rotation-sequence rule holds for any k x k quadrant, and the factory reads k from the red block (probe 385/385).

objects.why: One binary 2x2 pattern, so only 14 possibilities.

placement.why: The three-quadrant sequence with a red placeholder is the task's structure in every fixture.

density_colours.why: Ink 1 on 0 plus red 2 are fixture roles; 1..3 of 4 cells are lit (30).

rule_parameters.why: Continue the clockwise rotation sequence.

demonstration_context.why: Query-only factory; the sequence is visible in the query. The finite certificate requires queries distinct from demonstrations.

be03b35f.proposal: High: tiny domain. Sample quadrant size k in 2..9 with a gap of 1..3 (canvas 2k+gap <= 30) and keep binary ink; recertify. Until then admit only under finite-domain identity rules.
be03b35f.uncertainties: Whether quadrants larger than 2x2, or multi-colour quadrants, belong to the original task; no fixture shows them. Rotation-symmetric patterns make some quadrants identical, and how often that confuses solvers was not measured.

c35c1b4c.mechanism: A 10x10 grid of noise drawn from two colours plus black (line 35). A foreground blob of a third colour grows from (4,4) within rows 1-8 and cols 0-4, and each added cell is mirrored into the right half with probability 1/2 (lines 36-48). The output mirrors every left-half foreground cell onto the right half and keeps the existing right-half cells (lines 54-56). This completes a left-right symmetric blob.
c35c1b4c.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 10x10, 4 colours each (pair 0: 0/3/7/9, foreground 3). Every output completes the blob symmetrically about the vertical centre line; e.g. pair 3's row 4 becomes all 9. Audit native: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: 10 is a literal in the canvas, the growth bounds and the mirror index (9 - c). The factory needs only even dimensions with a central 2x2 block.

objects.why: One blob of 18-24 growth steps, seeded at (4,4) and kept off the top and bottom rows. Anchoring at the centre is rule-supported; the sizes are incidental.

placement.why: Growth is confined to the left half, and right-half cells exist only as mirrors. The mirror axis is always vertical natively; D4 augmentation varies it at episode level.

density_colours.why: Three distinct non-zero colours plus black, with the foreground excluded from the noise. These are rule roles, preserved under the palette.

rule_parameters.why: Natively, the foreground is the colour at (4,4) and the axis is vertical. The factory keeps 8 hypotheses: 4 central cells x 2 axes.

demonstration_context.why: The factory solve keeps the central-cell and axis hypotheses that fit every demonstration and raises unless they agree on the query. The certificate records 26 context retries.

c35c1b4c.proposal: Medium: sample even H and W (8-16), seed at a central cell, and scale growth with the half-area. Optionally vary which central cell seeds the blob, provided the hypothesis class stays identifiable. Recertify.
c35c1b4c.uncertainties: Unknown: whether the original rule picks the foreground by centre position or by another cue (e.g. the largest symmetric object). The factory's hypothesis class is a modelling choice.

dimensions.why: Literal 3x3 canvas: the self-tiling pattern. The bound is 3H, 3W <= 30, and the teacher reads h and w (probe 400/400).

objects.why: There are no objects; 3..4 colours (28) is narrower than what the rule admits.

placement.why: The whole grid is copied into each block, so cell positions only matter through the flips.

density_colours.why: Uniform cells over the chosen colours with no 0, matching the fixtures.

rule_parameters.why: Mirrored 3x3 tiling: rows flipped in even block-rows, columns flipped in even block-columns.

demonstration_context.why: The certified teacher transform reads only the query grid, never the demonstrations, and nothing in the rule depends on episode context.

c48954c1.proposal: Medium. Sample H, W independently in 1..10 and 2..9 colours; recertify.
c48954c1.uncertainties: Mirroring is defined for any shape, but no fixture shows a non-square input.

c6e1b8da.mechanism: 3-5 solid rectangles (3-9 per side) in distinct colours on a 20x20 black canvas (lines 92-98). At least two have a one-cell-wide 'stick' of length 1-5 leaving one side away from the corners (lines 46-56, 99-102). The output slides each such box by its stick length in the stick's direction and removes the stick (lines 57-68). Draws are rejected if a pulled box would be overdrawn, any cell leaves the canvas, or any box shows fewer than 3 visible corners before or after the move (lines 44, 55, 62, 67, 70-88).
c6e1b8da.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 20x20. In pair 0 the orange box has a 2-cell downward stick at col 9 (rows 7-8) and has moved down 2 in the output. Still and moving boxes overlap, as in pair 1. Audit native: 128/128 unique, 4.3 s for 128 draws.

dimensions.why: 20 is a literal. The bound at line 62 is asymmetric: it rejects row+tall >= 20, so a moved box may touch the top or left edge but never the bottom or right. Input boxes never touch any edge (lines 97-98).

objects.why: 3-5 boxes with at least 2 sticks match the fixtures. The box size ranges are incidental.

placement.why: The no-overdraw and at-least-3-corners guards keep every box recoverable from the input (rule-supported). Overlap with still boxes is allowed.

density_colours.why: Distinct box colours identify objects, which the per-colour analysis in the factory relies on.

rule_parameters.why: Each box shifts by its stick length toward the stick. The 'down' offset keeps sticks off corners (line 101), so the stick side is unambiguous.

demonstration_context.why: The factory reads demonstrations only to reject contradictory ones; the answer comes from the query alone (_recover). Ambiguous queries are rejected by the admission gate (certificate audit_scope).

c6e1b8da.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (14-26) with scaled bounds, and fix the >= 20 off-by-one so moved boxes may touch every edge. Recertify.
c6e1b8da.uncertainties: Not measured: whether the edge asymmetry is visible at episode level after D4 augmentation, and acceptance rates at other sizes.

c7d4e6ad.mechanism: A 10x10 black canvas with a colour legend in column 0: 2-4 distinct non-grey colours in segments of 1-4 rows, 7-8 rows in total (lines 29-40). A connected grey (5) shape starting at column 3 grows in random segments until every legend row contains grey (lines 42-69). The output recolours every non-black cell with its row's legend colour (lines 75-77).
c7d4e6ad.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, 10x10. Pair 0's legend 9,9,6,6,6,4,4,4 recolours the grey shape row by row. In all pairs the grey starts at column 3 and stays within columns 3-7, matching native widths 3-5. Audit native: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: The 10x10 canvas and the 7-8 legend height are literals.

objects.why: A single grey shape is required to be connected (line 69), which is rule-supported. It is built from random runs; its 3-5 width is incidental.

placement.why: Grey covers every legend row (lines 58-62), so every grey cell has a defined colour (rule-supported). The fixed start column 3 is incidental.

density_colours.why: Legend colours are distinct and exclude grey, and the segment lengths sum to the legend height.

rule_parameters.why: Recolour each cell by its row's column-0 colour.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained; the factory does not read demonstrations.

c7d4e6ad.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (8-16), a legend height up to H-2, and the grey start column and width; optionally allow 2-6 legend colours. Recertify.
c7d4e6ad.uncertainties: Unknown: whether grey rows outside the legend span belong to the original task (native forbids them).

ca8de6ea.mechanism: A 5x5 X of five distinct non-zero colours (28) on 0: corners, inner diagonal ring and centre (31-35). The X compresses into a solid 3x3: corners stay corners, the centre stays the centre, and the inner ring turns onto the edge midpoints (31-35).
ca8de6ea.fixture_evidence: 4 pairs (3 train, 1 test), 5x5 -> 3x3, all with one geometry. finite_input_policy.py (lines 95-100) registers the family: 9P5 = 15,120 inputs in one palette/D4 orbit. Audit: 127/128 unique, 1 orbit; certificate: 968/1000.

dimensions.why: Fixed 5x5 -> 3x3. The factory hard-codes the nine source cells. No fixture shows another X size, and how a 7x7 X with three rings would compress is undefined.

objects.why: One X motif of nine cells is the whole task, as in every fixture.

placement.why: The X geometry (corners, inner diagonal ring, centre) is fixed by the rule and the factory.

density_colours.why: Five distinct non-zero colours, as in every fixture.

rule_parameters.why: A fixed cell-to-cell compression of the nine X cells into the 3x3 block.

demonstration_context.why: The factory's solve() reads only the query grid, never the demonstrations, and nothing in the rule depends on episode context.

ca8de6ea.proposal: Medium, blocked on semantics. Keep the constructor and admit only under the existing finite_input_policy entry (exact-input identity, four distinct inputs per episode). Any larger X would invent rules that no fixture shows.
ca8de6ea.uncertainties: Whether repeated colours within the X are allowed (every fixture uses five distinct colours).

ce039d91.mechanism: This is the native repair (1ed7790/5436f3f). The width is even, 4-30, and the height is 3-30 (lines 34-37). Black must stay modal and both outcomes must appear (line 52). There are 1000 proposals.

dimensions.why: Height is 3-30 and width is even, 4-30. Even width is kept as a rule boundary: an odd width would add an undemonstrated self-mirror column.

objects.why: Pair and single rates are sampled per scene. Objects are pixels, not shapes, as in the fixtures.

placement.why: Mirrored placement about the vertical centre line is the rule's axis.

density_colours.why: The black-modal clause serves the archived verifier. Requiring both outcomes keeps the rule visible.

rule_parameters.why: A grey cell with a grey mirror becomes blue; otherwise it stays grey.

demonstration_context.why: The factory compares the query with its mirror and never reads demonstrations.

ce039d91.proposal: None. The expansion already removed the fixed canvas and certified it. Remaining work: rerun the stale audit on sha 73050bcc.
ce039d91.uncertainties: Whether odd widths, with a self-mirror centre column, belong to the original rule; no fixture shows one.

cf133acc.mechanism: A 15x15 black canvas. Two vertical stubs of length 1-6 stand at the bottom, one each side of a midline at 6-8 (lines 57-60). There are 2-6 horizontal bars, each running from the left (reaching mid or mid+1), from the right, or across the full width, with a gap at a stub column (lines 61-74, 52). Bars on the same side are non-adjacent, and both sides occur (lines 35-39). The output extends each stub to the top row, switching to each crossed bar's colour (lines 46-53).
cf133acc.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 15x15. Pair 0 has stubs 1 (col 3) and 5 (col 9), with bars 3 and 4 on the left and 6 and 7 on the right; output column 3 reads 3,3,3,3,4,4,4,4,4,1,... from the top. Audit native: 128/128 unique. Line 77 prints mid, hsides and hlengths to stdout on every native draw: a leftover debug print with no semantic effect.

dimensions.why: 15 is a literal throughout: the canvas, the right-side index 14 - col (line 43), the midline 6-8 and stub columns up to 13 (lines 57-58), and the full-width length 15 (line 74).

objects.why: Exactly two stubs (fixture-faithful, but incidental), and 2-6 bars.

placement.why: Both sides occur, same-side bars are non-adjacent, and each row has the same colour on both sides of a stub (lines 49-50). So every gap lies inside a bar and the colour switch is well defined (rule-supported).

density_colours.why: Bar colours are distinct and exclude the stub colours, so every crossing is visible.

rule_parameters.why: Moving upward from the bottom, each stub cell takes the colour of the last bar crossed.

demonstration_context.why: Self-contained; the factory does not read demonstrations.

cf133acc.proposal: Medium: sample H and W (11-20) and 1-3 stubs with bars aligned to them. Remove the debug print at line 77; it does not change outputs. Recertify.
cf133acc.uncertainties: Unknown: whether more than two stubs fit the original task. Not checked: whether the stdout print disturbs harnesses that capture output.

placement.why: The whole grid is copied with rotations.

density_colours.why: The 8 role is literal at p 2/3, matching the fixtures; other proportions are not sampled.

rule_parameters.why: Fixed quadrant rotations (180, clockwise, anticlockwise, identity), each quadrant tiled 2x2.

demonstration_context.why: The factory's solve() reads only the query grid, never the demonstrations, and nothing in the rule depends on episode context.

cf5fd0ad.proposal: Medium. Sample square n in 2..7 and an 8-share per scene; recertify.
cf5fd0ad.uncertainties: Whether non-square inputs belong to the task; no fixture shows one, and the rotations would change shape.

e45ef808.mechanism: A 12x12 grid: a black top row, a blue field, and grey-6 bars rising from the bottom, one per column. Bar lengths are 1-7 from a random walk and need at least 5 distinct values (lines 27-38). In the output, the rightmost tallest bar's column gets yellow 4 above the bar (lines 47-51), and the leftmost shortest bar's column gets maroon 9 (lines 53-57).
e45ef808.fixture_evidence: 3 canonical pairs, all 12x12. Distinct lengths per pair: 6, 5, 5. probes/fixture_stats_batch4.py (seed 0) finds a tied tallest only in train[1], where cols 7 and 11 both have length 5 and col 11 gets the 4. No canonical pair has a tied shortest. In native draws, tallest is tied in 1138/2000 and shortest in 1100/2000. Audit: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: The literal 12 sets both the column count and the height. The rule (mark the extreme bars) works on any H×W with headroom.

objects.why: One contiguous bar per column is rule-supported. The 1-7 cap (keeping at least 4 blue rows) and the at-least-5-distinct guard are literals that match the fixtures.

placement.why: Bottom-anchored bars are rule-supported. The smooth ±1/±2 walk profile (lines 33-35) is incidental.

density_colours.why: Blue background, black top row, grey bars and the 4/9 markers are all literals. They vary only through the episode palette.

rule_parameters.why: The tallest bar's column gets 4 above it and the shortest bar's column gets 9. The >= and <= comparisons fix the tie-breaks: rightmost tallest, leftmost shortest.

demonstration_context.why: Natively, the leftmost-shortest tie-break decides about 55% of draws, but no canonical pair demonstrates it. The rightmost-tallest tie-break is shown once (train[1]). The factory hard-codes both tie-breaks (SIGN), so episodes without a tie never reveal the convention.

e45ef808.proposal: Medium. Sample H and W (columns 5-30; height at least max length + 2) and scale the length cap with height (lines 29, 37). Either reject shortest ties (closest to the fixtures) or ensure some demonstration shows one. Recertify.
e45ef808.uncertainties: The original task's shortest tie-break is unknown, since no canonical pair has a shortest tie. The reason for the at-least-5-distinct guard is unknown. Episode-level tie coverage was not measured.

e5c44e8f.mechanism: An 11x11 black grid with a green seed at rows/columns 4-6 and 0-10 random red pixels (lines 30-41). Green grows a square spiral from the seed: up first, then clockwise, with segment lengths 2, 2, 4, 4, ... (lines 42-56). Each step is drawn only if the cell is not red; the first red cell stops the spiral, and off-canvas steps are skipped (common.draw). The loop is capped at 21 segments (line 43).
e5c44e8f.fixture_evidence: 4 canonical pairs, 11x11. Red counts are 9, 0, 10 and 10; seeds are (5,5), (4,5), (4,4) and (5,6). In train[1] there are no reds, so the spiral runs past every edge and row 10 is all green. Audit: 123/128 unique. Draws with 0 reds (probability 1/11) leave only the 9 seed positions, which explains the duplicates.

dimensions.why: The canvas is a literal 11x11, and the seed range and 21-segment cap are tuned to it. On a larger canvas the cap would cut the spiral short; the factory's cap scales as 4*(H+W)+8.

objects.why: One seed and some red obstacles are rule-supported. The 0-10 count is a literal; duplicates and a red under the seed (overwritten at line 41) silently lower the effective count.

placement.why: Reds are uniform anywhere. The seed is held near the centre (4-6), which matches the fixtures but is tied to the canvas.

density_colours.why: Red 2, green 3 and black background are literals; they vary only through the palette.

rule_parameters.why: A clockwise square spiral from the seed, with segment lengths growing by 2 every other turn, stopped by the first red.

demonstration_context.why: The start direction (up) and turn sense are fixed natively. The factory maps them per d4 (DIRS), reads only the query, and never touches demonstrations.

e5c44e8f.proposal: Medium. Sample H and W, let the seed range scale with the canvas, and replace the 21-segment cap (line 43) with a canvas-derived bound. Recertify.
e5c44e8f.uncertainties: Whether the seed must be central in the original is unknown; the canonical seeds are 4-6. Spiral truncation at larger sizes was not measured.

fd02da9e.mechanism: An 8x8 orange-7 grid. Each corner, independently with probability 1/2, holds a distinct colour from 1-9, with 7 remapped to 0; at least one corner must be set (lines 27-38). The output removes the corner pixels and stamps fixed templates: 2x2 squares at (1-2,1-2) and (1-2,5-6) for the top corners, and 3-cell hooks (4,2), (5,2), (6,3) and (4,5), (5,5), (6,4) for the bottom corners (lines 39-42).
fd02da9e.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, 8x8. Each train pair has exactly one set corner (bottom-left 1, top-right 8, bottom-right 0, top-left 9); the test pair sets all four. probes/fixture_stats_batch4.py counts the native domain exactly: 5508 inputs over only 15 corner-occupancy patterns. Audit: 112/128 unique, 5 orbits.

dimensions.why: 8x8 is a literal and the templates sit at absolute offsets. No fixture shows whether, on a larger canvas, they stay corner-anchored (as the factory's OFFS assume) or converge on the centre.

objects.why: The top-corner and bottom-corner templates differ, as in the canonical pairs.

placement.why: Seeds exist only at the four corners (lines 35-38); there are no interior seeds.

density_colours.why: Distinct corner colours on orange are rule-supported. The 1/2 occupancy is a literal.

rule_parameters.why: A fixed output template per corner: 2x2 squares for the top corners, 3-cell hooks for the bottom corners.

demonstration_context.why: Each corner's template is a convention learnt only from pairs that use that corner. Canonical train shows each corner once; native episodes may lack a demo for the query's corner. The factory hard-codes OFFS.

fd02da9e.proposal: High. The structural domain is 15 occupancy patterns on one fixed geometry. Any canvas generalisation must first settle how the templates are anchored (unknown), so no patch is justified yet. Resolve the semantics, then sample H and W and recertify. Meanwhile, an episode policy could ensure every query corner appears in a demo.
fd02da9e.uncertainties: How the templates are anchored on larger canvases. Episode-level corner coverage was not measured.

ff2825db.mechanism: A 10x10 grid: a fixed legend row 0 '1122334455'; a 10x9 hollow frame in fg colour at row 1; and a 7x8 interior of clutter in two colours drawn inside a random box (lines 28-36, 58-76). Clutter needs exactly 2 colours (line 38), a unique mode colour (line 43) and a mode bounding box of at least 2x2 (line 54). The output recolours the frame to the mode colour, clears the interior, and draws a hollow rectangle on the mode cells' bounding box (lines 44-55).
ff2825db.fixture_evidence: 5 canonical pairs, 10x10. Train[3]'s mode colour 4 has 2 cells whose bounding box is exactly 2x2, which is the line-54 boundary. Line 65 swaps the bounds: brow comes from 0..8-wide and bcol from 0..7-tall. Line 68 silently skips rows and columns past the interior. probes/fixture_stats_batch4.py computes that 42.9% of line-64/65 parameter draws give a clipped clutter box, biasing clutter toward the bottom and right. The scenes stay valid. Audit: 128/128 unique.

dimensions.why: The literal 10x10 canvas, the 10x9 frame and the 7x8 interior.

objects.why: Two clutter colours with a unique mode and a non-degenerate bounding box are rule-supported. The 2-8 by 2-7 clutter box is a literal.

placement.why: The clutter box sits anywhere in the interior, but line 65 pairs brow with wide and bcol with tall. This is a latent defect: harmless for validity, but it biases toward clipped boxes (42.9%).

density_colours.why: Clutter frequencies 1/(1+freq) per scene vary widely. Colours come only from 1-5, matching the legend row; fg and clutter colours are distinct.

rule_parameters.why: The frame takes the mode colour, and a hollow box is drawn on the mode's bounding box.

demonstration_context.why: The factory recomputes the mode inside the fixed frame bounds for each query and never reads demonstrations.

ff2825db.proposal: Medium. Fix line 65 (brow over 0..7-tall, bcol over 0..8-wide), then sample the canvas and frame size. Recertify.
ff2825db.uncertainties: Whether the legend row means anything in the original or is decorative; the rule never reads it. The effect of the line-65 skew on the final bounding-box distribution was not measured.
